_comment: One `editor` request, blocking, with NO self_resolve_ms — and the omission is the entire scenario. SRD §4.2 gives select/confirm/input an optional timeout that resolves them on their own; `editor` has none, so an unanswered one hangs the agent forever and the supervisor's timer is the only unblocker. That is ISC-112, and it is the one UI criterion ISA.md records as more likely to be FALSE in production than merely unproven: against a supervisor with no responder, this turn blocks until deadline_s expires and settles timed_out / deadline_exceeded_no_terminal_event, which is the kill ladder working correctly and is exactly what "hangs the run" means. Giving this dialog a self_resolve_ms would model the one behaviour `editor` provably does not have, and would turn the probe green on the fixture's own timer while the criterion stayed false — the false pass ISA.md warns about in as many words. So the double hangs here indefinitely, on purpose: a run that reaches turn_end proves a supervisor answered, and a run that does not says so in its verdict rather than in a test timeout. The `params` mirror a real editor invocation (a file to open, seeded content) so the log line a human reads afterwards says what was actually being asked for.
